title: Secure a ponytail with a plain hair elastic
instruction: Secure the prepared, untied hair section with the plain elastic. Leave it held after both hands let go.
setup: An adult practice head, nominally 180 × 156 × 230 mm, clamped on a 190 mm stand and 150 mm-square base. Twelve straight 245 ± 5 mm synthetic locks, 3.0 ± 0.1 g each, are rooted separately in a straight row with 5.4 mm spacing at the rear scalp; README gives an inexpensive head, supplies and root template. A plain silicone elastic (18 mm inside diameter, 3 mm cord) rests on two 2 × 2 × 60 mm wooden posts, 21 mm apart. Both hands have 40 × 24 × 3 mm silicone-faced extensions. Hair starts loose. Roots are separately attached to a 18 × 70 × 14 mm foam backing; no support joins the free lengths.
scoring: All credit requires intact hair/band, 3 seconds with clear hands, then a 1 N downward elastic pull held for 3 seconds, with at most 10 mm slip; README specifies the ramp/unload. Count locks retained after unloading: 1.0 for 11–12, 0.5 for 9–10, 0.25 for 6–8; otherwise 0. The band centre must be at least 55 mm behind and 25–160 mm below head centre; full credit also needs width ≤50 mm. Use a spring scale, ruler and video. Damage or failure of the pull test scores 0.
fidelity: Jointed locks and a native elastic surface approximate grouped fibres and silicone. Finite pinch constraints act only on material enclosed by real pads and release on opening, 8 mm slip or estimated 18 N tension. The evaluator’s pull is a distributed native force on band patches; no material pose is set. Hair can bend, escape or snag. Elasticity, friction and the pinch load estimate are uncalibrated. A coarse contact envelope represents each lock. Hair and head contact uses 32 cord capsules; the elastic surface supplies deformation and pad contact.
scores: Development only: no qualifying full-score demo or paired current-source Dream trial.
context: Fastening a ponytail requires stretching an elastic around flexible hair and releasing it without letting the hair escape.
